clue.text: Look at what's in popular detergent

indicators.note: 's in reads as 'is in', so the first word sits inside the brand name that follows

parts.note: Bold is a well-known British brand of washing powder
'Eh?' is a way of saying 'What?'

explanation.surface: An advert inviting shoppers to see what goes into a favourite washing powder.
explanation.walkthrough: Bold is a British laundry detergent brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Behold is an old-fashioned imperative meaning see or observe, used just like the command 'Look!'

clue.text: Wrong head chopped off monster

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the following word is removed

parts.note: a terror is a frightening person or creature

explanation.surface: A grisly tale of a beast beheaded by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the T from TERROR to leave ERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong, as a noun, is a mistake or fault, which is what an error is.

clue.text: Unusually virtuous nurses died, though not at first

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold or cradle, so one word holds the other inside it
not at first tells us the opening letter of the combined result is dropped

parts.note: godly means devout and good
d is the standard abbreviation for died in records

explanation.surface: A saintly nurse has lost a patient, though not at the start of the shift.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside GODLY to make GODDLY, then the G is dropped to leave ODDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs describe something happening in a strange or unexpected manner.

clue.text: Casually draws lots after onset of dispute

indicators.note: the onset of something is its beginning, so take only the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of dispute
oodles is an informal word for a great quantity

explanation.surface: Someone settles an argument by drawing lots once it starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws lots' looks like a single phrase about chance; draws belongs to the definition and lots is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To doodle is to sketch idly and absent-mindedly, i.e. to draw casually.

clue.text: Come across useless type of horse

parts.note: bum as an adjective means worthless or of poor quality
a pinto is a piebald or skewbald horse

explanation.surface: A disappointed rider encounters a worthless kind of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into someone is an idiom for meeting them by chance, i.e. to come across them.

clue.text: I throw up going through country

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to lob is to toss something in a high arc
via means by way of or passing through

explanation.surface: A traveller confesses to vomiting while crossing a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' reads as being sick, but throw and up do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a landlocked nation in South America.

clue.text: Serious about island resort

parts.note: major means important or serious, as in a major problem
ca is the abbreviation of circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: Someone is in earnest about a holiday on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is a Spanish Balearic island famous as a package-holiday destination.

clue.text: Generous fellow's after stylish flat? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite all of the word is used, so its final letter is cut

parts.note: in means fashionable
flat in the sense of lifeless or uninteresting
gent is short for gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A kindly man is living in a fashionable apartment, or almost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' wants to be an apartment; here it means dull, which loses its last L.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulgent means lenient and lavish in granting wishes, which is a kind of generosity.

clue.text: Aristotle redesigned machine for the better

indicators.note: a redesign changes the layout, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Greek philosopher reworked into a device that improves things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the better' reads as improvement, but a better here is someone who places bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A totaliser, or tote, is the machine that pools wagers and calculates payouts for gamblers at racecourses.

clue.text: Spring containing unrefined petroleum

indicators.note: containing means the first item holds the next inside it

parts.note: a coil is a spiral spring
rude in the old sense of rough and unpolished

explanation.surface: A natural spring yielding untreated oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unrefined petroleum' reads as one phrase, and it also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude oil is petroleum in its natural state as extracted from the ground.

clue.text: Book a lot of combat sport, then hit deceptively

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, means the word loses its end

parts.note: judo is a Japanese martial art

indicators.note: acting deceptively disguises things, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A martial-arts manual, with tips on landing sneaky blows.
explanation.walkthrough: JUDO loses its O, then HIT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Judith is a book of the Apocrypha, included in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles.

clue.text: Bird that greatly enjoys fruit, so it's said

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so we want a phrase that sounds like the answer when spoken

parts.note: someone very fond of a fruit that grows in bunches

explanation.surface: A bird known for its passion for fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey plover is a wading shorebird of coasts and estuaries.

clue.text: Ultimate in retro features in 50s lounge

indicators.note: to feature in something is to appear within it

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so several fifties give a run of Ls

indicators.note: the ultimate part of a word is its very end, so take its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of retro

explanation.surface: Retro styling is a feature of a 1950s lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: '50s' looks like the decade, but it means Roman fifties: O sits after the first L of LLL.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to lounge or sprawl lazily.

clue.text: Divine food aromas I prepared with a pinch of basil

indicators.note: food that is prepared is worked on, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a pinch is a tiny amount, just the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of basil

explanation.surface: A cook boasts of a heavenly dish seasoned with fragrant herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ambrosia was the food of the gods, conferring immortality.

clue.text: Soul's crushed, gathered by small 22

indicators.note: being gathered by something means being held within it

parts.note: mini means small

indicators.note: something crushed is broken up, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the possessive taken as its letters

explanation.surface: A tyrant's spirit is broken by petty followers.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit inside MINI after its M. 22 refers to the answer at 22-across, a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Benito Mussolini was Italy's Fascist dictator, an absolute ruler.

clue.text: Narrowing I have on pipe overhead

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a duct is a tube or channel
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: A plumber complains of a constriction in the pipework above.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'overhead' puts the first two pieces above the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Reductive means simplifying or limiting something too much, as a narrowing adjective.

clue.text: Relaxed one behaving like 20D?

parts.note: a means one
Delilah, the answer at 20-down, beguiled Samson, which is the behaviour of a temptress

explanation.surface: A woman who lures men on stays perfectly calm about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The spaces move: 'a tease' becomes 'at ease'.
explanation.definitionFit: At ease is an idiom for comfortable and free from tension.

clue.text: Quiet words in leading songs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: remarks muttered so others do not hear
second meaning: the main tracks on vinyl singles, written A-sides

explanation.surface: Whispered lyrics in the opening numbers of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside is a remark made in an undertone; an A-side is the featured track of a record single.

clue.text: Disease afflicted surfers here?

indicators.note: something afflicted is troubled and disordered, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An illness struck the surfing crowd at their beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast by the sea is where surfers would naturally be found riding waves.

clue.text: Cherry pie stuffed with small bird

indicators.note: something stuffed is filled, so a letter goes inside the word

parts.note: cherry red is a colour
a tart is a pastry pie
S is the abbreviation for small in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A cherry pie with a little bird baked inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small bird' looks like one phrase; small is the letter and bird alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a small songbird with a reddish tail.

clue.text: "Carry On Jack" shown during holiday

indicators.note: something shown during a period sits inside it

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday
jack and tar are both old words for a sailor

explanation.surface: An old comedy film is screened on a bank holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry On Jack is a 1963 film in Britain's Carry On comedy series, which hides the definition in a title.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to resume or begin again after stopping, i.e. to carry on.

clue.text: Cheered up after capturing large biblical character

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading from bottom to top
capturing something means holding it inside

parts.note: hailed means acclaimed or cheered
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A crowd cheers up after taking a big prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed word takes L after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Delilah is the woman in the Book of Judges who betrayed Samson.

clue.text: Actor performs, but not with a metal band

indicators.note: performing involves acting things out in new shapes, so the letters are rearranged
not with means without, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer plays without a heavy metal group backing him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metal band' suggests a rock group, but it is a ring of metal. Remove an A from ACTOR and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A torc is an ancient Celtic neck ring of twisted metal.

clue.text: Tyrant musician going after sailor like this

parts.note: AB stands for able seaman
so means in this way
a lutist plays the lute

explanation.surface: A domineering musician pursues a sailor in this manner.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolutist favours absolute, unlimited power, as a despot does.

clue.text: It's shaped like a doughnut? Sounds like bull

indicators.note: sounds like tells us to match pronunciation rather than spelling

parts.note: Taurus is the bull of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A guessing game: is it ring-shaped? It sounds like a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a torus is the ring-shaped surface of a ring doughnut or inner tube.

clue.text: Squeeze inside clothing for severe criticism

indicators.note: inside places one item within the other
clothing is the outer covering, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the clue's opening word
to nip is to pinch or squeeze

explanation.surface: Tight clothing draws harsh comments.
explanation.walkthrough: Squeeze does double duty: as NIP, and as its own outer letters S and E around that.
explanation.definitionFit: A snipe is a sharp, critical remark, a piece of harsh criticism.

clue.text: Starts to boost intimate relations with one's skimpy garment

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: first letters of these two words
kin are relatives
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A daring swimsuit is meant to spice up a couple's love life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate relations' looks like a phrase about sex, but the words split between two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece swimsuit that covers very little.

clue.text: Each son of Trump admits government is hypersensitive

parts.note: all in the sense of every one

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Eric Trump is one of Donald Trump's sons
G is a common abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: Every Trump son lets politics in and is oversensitive about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric is one of Donald Trump's sons.
explanation.definitionFit: Being allergic means reacting badly to a substance, an immune system that overreacts, so hypersensitive.

clue.text: Emergency equipment beginning to look festive at sea

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of look

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Safety gear on a cruise ship starts to look like party wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A life vest is a buoyant jacket worn to keep someone afloat in a disaster on water.

clue.text: Possesses permit for meat

parts.note: has means owns
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A butcher holds a licence to sell meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Haslet is a British meatloaf of pork offal and herbs, served cold in slices.
explanation.definitionFit: Haslet is a kind of cooked pork meatloaf, so it is a type of meat.
